_about: Where each proposed setting puts the places Clark's ten points name, from public sources only (lab.geography2 step 2), written 2026-11-22 before any grading. A place with no public placement is left out and the points that need it are reported 'cannot grade'. Sorenson's place-by-place placements (An Ancient American Setting, 1985; Mormon's Codex, 2013) are not used: not replicated until the books are bought. Points are lat, lon; a river is a Natural Earth river name. 'note' says where each came from.

narrow neck.note: Isthmus of Tehuantepec (Clark 1989 on Sorenson); point on its narrowest line, finalisation

east sea.note: Gulf of Mexico off Coatzacoalcos (the sea across the isthmus from the Pacific)

Cumorah.note: Cerro El Vigia, Wikipedia 'Cumorah' (proposed by some Latter-day Saint scholars)

narrow neck.note: Niagara peninsula (Wikipedia 'Hypothetical setting', Great Lakes table)

Cumorah.note: Hill Cumorah near Palmyra, New York (same table)

Nephi.note: 'the Appalachian region of Tennessee' (same article); Knoxville as its point, finalisation

waters of Mormon.note: 'the springs of northern Georgia just south of Chattanooga' (same article)

narrow neck.note: Isthmus of Panama (Wikipedia 'Hypothetical setting', Hemispheric table)

Cumorah.note: Hill Cumorah, New York (same article: early readers placed the last battle there)
